metadata.notes: Source-led anniversary research with local-date precision and independently described alternate weather stories; document survey and publisher dependence.

reviews.title_after: European windstorm Vivian forms before devastating winds sweep the continent
reviews.core_fact: The European windstorm Vivian was developing by February 25, 1990; its most extreme overland winds followed on February 26.
reviews.source_dependence: European Windstorms reanalysis and the peer-reviewed Dutch storm-surge study use differing storm metrics, but both rely partly on shared reanalysis and national observational archives.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Feb25 is the cyclone's development/onset phase, not the date of peak 925-hPa reanalysis wind (Feb26). Do not equate Vivian with Wiebke on Feb28, or transfer multinational economic losses to Feb25.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original European cyclone MSLP/925-hPa wind-track diagram with dated onset and peak markers

reviews.title_before: Tornado — ESTILL MUNI ARPT, South Carolina
reviews.title_after: A damaging F2 tornado tracks through downtown Iowa City
reviews.core_fact: A damaging tornado struck Iowa City, Iowa during the evening of April 13, 2006, as part of a larger eastern Iowa/western Illinois outbreak.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS survey establishes the F2 and Iowa City path; contemporaneous Radio Iowa independently documented campus/city damage while quoting NWS forecasters; both ultimately share outbreak-survey information.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Official rating was historical F2, not EF2 (EF scale began 2007); distinguish 30 Iowa City injuries from separate Nichols fatality and contemporaneous preliminary F3 spotter reports. April 12, 2020 Bassfield EF4 on neighboring anniversary is a separate event.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Iowa City historical tornado path over a simplified streets/campus map with survey path boundaries

reviews.title_after: Historic northwest Iowa floodwaters continue downstream after days of intense rain
reviews.location_after: Big Sioux and Little Sioux basins, northwestern Iowa
reviews.core_fact: River flooding persisted in parts of northwestern Iowa on June 25, 2024, following torrential rainfall June 20–22; NWS flood warnings remained in effect as waters routed downstream.
reviews.source_dependence: USGS independent streamgage research and the original NWS June25 flood warning document distinct hydrologic measurements and operational forecast status, although both use shared gauge data.
reviews.unverified_cautions: June25 is a continuation/routing anniversary, NOT the heaviest rain or universal peak crest. Rock River, West Fork Des Moines and Little Sioux crests varied by gauge and day; do not transfer a June24 or June27 crest to June25.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original basin river-route map with selected station hydrographs and explicit crest dates

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Arthur makes a late-night Category 2 landfall on North Carolina's coast
reviews.location_after: Shackleford Banks, Carteret County, North Carolina
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Arthur made landfall near Shackleford Banks, North Carolina at about 11:15 p.m. EDT July 3, 2014, as a Category 2 hurricane.
reviews.source_dependence: NHC near-real-time center fix documents the precise local timestamp, while North Carolina State Climate Office separately contextualized the impacts and local records based partly on the NHC analysis.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The same landfall was 0315 UTC on JULY 4; do not confuse UTC/EDT or describe July4 local landfall. The storm crossed Shackleford Banks west of Cape Lookout, not the more northern Outer Banks first.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original local-vs-UTC timeline and coastal landfall track with tide/observation timestamps

reviews.title_after: A microburst strikes departing Pan Am Flight 759 near New Orleans
reviews.location_after: New Orleans International Airport and Kenner, Louisiana
reviews.core_fact: On July 9, 1982, Pan Am Flight 759 encountered microburst-related wind shear during takeoff from New Orleans International Airport, a central finding of the NTSB accident investigation.
reviews.source_dependence: NTSB accident reconstruction is original investigation; FAA educational account interprets the same NTSB findings and thus is not independent measurement corroboration; historic UPI tower-transcript reporting supports chronology.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not confuse this 1982 *takeoff* microburst with August 2, 1985 Delta 191 *approach* microburst already on calendar. Wind shear alert/crew warning timing and radar detection need line-level checking in NTSB report; avoid assigning a single aircraft performance factor as only cause.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original vertical microburst cross-section showing takeoff track, headwind-to-tailwind loss and downdraft

reviews.title_after: Rare Labor Day east winds accelerate catastrophic Oregon wildfires
reviews.location_after: Western Oregon and the Cascade Range
reviews.core_fact: An unusually strong easterly wind event began in western Oregon on September 7, 2020, rapidly spreading existing fires and contributing to new fire activity.
reviews.source_dependence: USGS public chronology and independent peer-reviewed compound-extremes analysis support weather sequence; NASA dated satellite imagery supplies a different observational domain, while fire impact estimates may share agencies.
reviews.unverified_cautions: September 7–9 was a multiday wind-driven spread period, not one simultaneous ignition at every fire. Downslope wind, low relative humidity and preexisting fuel conditions interact; avoid assuming wind directly ignited each blaze. Distinguish from September9 orange Bay Area skies primary.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Cascades cross-section of east-wind downslope drying and dated wildfire growth

reviews.title_after: Hurricane Floyd's remnants inundate New Jersey and the Raritan basin
reviews.location_after: Somerset County and Raritan River basin, New Jersey
reviews.core_fact: Hurricane Floyd and a stalled front produced severe rain and flooding across central and northern New Jersey on September 16, 1999, including Somerset County and the Raritan basin.
reviews.source_dependence: NCEI Somerset County local flood report and NWS state flood history share NOAA historical sourcing, while Delaware River Basin Commission provides cross-agency river/watershed analysis outside the Raritan catchment.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Somerset County event record begins Sept16 and ends Sept18; do not treat segment-level damage or fatalities as New Jersey totals. Raritan and Delaware basin gauge/crest records cannot be merged into one river or one flood time.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Somerset/Raritan watershed flood route with rainfall date window and river peak day differentiation

reviews.title_after: An EF3 tornado strikes Nappanee, Indiana, in a major fall severe-weather outbreak
reviews.location_after: Nappanee and northwest Kosciusko County, Indiana
reviews.core_fact: An EF3 tornado struck Nappanee, Indiana late on October 18, 2007 during a multistate severe-weather outbreak.
reviews.source_dependence: Original NWS Northern Indiana detailed survey and Purdue Midwestern Regional Climate Center seasonal narrative corroborate occurrence, but the final EF3 intensity comes from shared NWS damage survey.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Distinguish Nappanee Indiana EF3 from separately surveyed Owensboro Kentucky EF3 the same evening, which is first alternate on this date; they occurred in the same parent severe-weather outbreak but not the same tornado. Do not conflate warning time, tornado time and overall multi-day outbreak totals.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Nappanee surveyed track plus storm warning timeline; avoid unlicensed historical damage photos

alternate_reviews.title: EF3 tornado strikes Owensboro, Kentucky
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: NCEI source segment and NWS Paducah long-form retrospective share the underlying tornado damage survey; Purdue MRCC is a separate publisher, not an independent F-scale instrument.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: An EF3 tornado damaged Owensboro, Kentucky on October 18, 2007, separate from the Nappanee, Indiana EF3.
alternate_reviews.caution: Both tornadoes belonged to the wider October18 2007 outbreak: different tornado tracks but related synoptic system; NOT a fully distinct outbreak alternative. Paducah's local time, the NCEI date, and UTC rollover need separate treatment.

alternate_reviews.title: Puget Sound October 2007 windstorm damages Seattle-area infrastructure
alternate_reviews.source_dependence: NOAA NCEI local storm segment was supplied from newspaper reports; Seattle P-I firsthand contemporaneous reporting confirms event/date but is potentially an underlying source of NCEI segment; not independent instrument observation.
alternate_reviews.core_fact: Strong winds caused power outages and storm damage in Seattle and the wider Puget Sound region on October 18, 2007.
alternate_reviews.caution: Avoid treating a single Seattle/Bremerton NCEI 48-knot zone magnitude as a region-wide station maximum, or counting the same Lake Washington incident twice. This is a separate West Coast windstorm from the Midwestern tornado outbreak.

editorial_deferrals: 04-13 2020 Estill EF4 from original single-source primary is verified in NCEI and NWS CHS, but would repeat the April12, 2020 Bassfield EF4 outbreak synoptic event; Iowa City 2006 selected instead.
07-09 1982 Pan Am 759 microburst is meteorologically similar to Aug02 Delta191; both distinct accidents, but avoid reused generic microburst diagrams.
06-25 2024 Iowa flooding is correctly timed as *ongoing river flooding*, not June25 precipitation maximum or any one universal crest.
10-18 Owensboro alternative shares the parent Oct18 2007 tornado outbreak with primary Nappanee, so editorial uniqueness is weaker even though distinct tornadoes.
